correctness.rationale: Reconstructed from D(n)=n sum_{p|n}vp(n)/p: set c=3a+2b, K=2^(a−1)*3^(b−2). Then D(n)=3Kc, D(phi(n))=K(c−2), phi(D(n))=Kc product_{q|c,q>=5}(1−1/q), yielding Euler-product deficit exactly 2. If any q>=5 divides c, deficit >=c/q; c=q gives deficit 1 and c=2q gives 2; no such q gives zero. Thus c=2q with q prime >=5; a even and q=3u+b. Dirichlet gives infinitude in the two reduced residue classes mod3 for fixed b, and none if 3|b. Counting interval 3u+2<=q<=X+u gives the exact prime-count sum; a uniform prime number theorem on u<=X/2 yields asymptotic X²/(4logX). Independently computed both arithmetic sides from factorizations for 225 exponent pairs (a,b in 2..16), all matched. Test scope excludes a<2,b<2.
